nodes.description: The normal protein is a single-domain TIM-barrel of the fold-type III PLP family that binds one PLP as an internal aldimine (Schiff base) on Lys47 and has no detected catalytic activity. Biallelic PLPBP variants remove this function in one of three ways. Nonsense, frameshift and canonical splice variants give no stable protein. Missense variants in the cofactor pocket (p.Val45Asp, p.Arg241Gln) give protein that is purified without PLP. Missense variants away from the pocket (p.Leu175Pro, p.Pro40Leu, p.Arg205Gln, p.Arg41Gln) misfold or destabilize the barrel. All three classes are loss of function; no variant has been shown to act as a gain of function or dominant negative, and heterozygous carriers are asymptomatic.

nodes.description: c.122G>A. Arg41 is on strand beta-1, 10.7 angstroms from PLP, and in the model makes a salt bridge to Glu220 and a hydrogen bond to Asn239, tying strand beta-1 to strands beta-7 and beta-8 where the barrel closes. It is not strictly conserved (lysine in several homologs, so the positive charge is the conserved feature). The variant protein is fully loaded with PLP but less thermostable, and patients are at the mild end of the spectrum. A stability variant with intact cofactor binding; p.Arg41Trp at the same residue is also reported.

nodes.description: c.370_373del. Frameshift at residue 124 with a stop two codons later, removing the C-terminal half of the barrel including the whole phosphate-binding site. The most frequently reported allele (18.5% of reported individuals) and a founder allele in the Saguenay-Lac-St-Jean region of Quebec. Homozygotes are at the severe end of the spectrum. gnomAD v4 allele frequency 6.7e-05 (108 of 1,614,058 alleles), the most common predicted loss-of-function allele in the gene.

evidence.reference_title: A founder mutation in the PLPBP gene in families from Saguenay-Lac-St-Jean region affected by a pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: Haplotype analysis showed a single shared profile for the affected persons and their parents, leading to a hypothesis about founder effect of the mutation in Saguenay-Lac-St-Jean region of French Canadians.

evidence.reference_title: Case report: PLPHP deficiency, a rare but important cause of B6-responsive disorders: A report of three novel individuals and review of 51 cases.
evidence.snippet: The eight individuals homozygous for this variant are at the severe end of the clinical spectrum with poor outcomes: six presented with a neonatal mitochondrial encephalopathy-like phenotype, and five died early in life (2 weeks to 16 months).

evidence.reference_title: Exploring the clinical, neuroimaging, and genetic spectrum of PLPBP deficiency: multicenter case series and systematic review.
evidence.snippet: The most common type of variant was missense variants (48%), with the variant c.370-373del being the most frequently reported (18.5%).

nodes.description: c.199G>A. Glu67 is invariant in all 29 other family sequences and fully buried (relative accessibility 0.00) at the end of strand beta-2, 6.9 angstroms from PLP. In the model its carboxylate bonds the backbone nitrogen of Lys47, the side chain of Ser46 and Lys76, so it positions the loop that carries the Schiff-base lysine. Lysine reverses the charge in a buried site. Consistent with a folding defect, this was the one variant that could not be produced in E. coli. ClinVar holds conflicting classifications for it.

nodes.description: c.275A>G. His92 is invariant in all 29 other family sequences and fully buried (relative accessibility 0.00) on strand beta-4, 8.6 angstroms from PLP, two residues before the PLP-contacting Ile94. Found in compound heterozygosity with p.Ala107Thr in a patient whose seizures began at eight months, the latest onset reported. Ala107 is exposed (relative accessibility 0.48), 19.8 angstroms from PLP and poorly conserved, so the structural case for p.Ala107Thr is weak and the late onset may reflect a mild second allele. Neither has been tested functionally; p.His92Arg is absent from ClinVar and p.Ala107Thr is a variant of uncertain significance there.

nodes.description: c.524T>C. Misfolding variant. In the model Leu175 is 18.8 angstroms from PLP, buried (relative accessibility 0.01) in barrel strand beta-6, and it is conserved in 26 of 29 other family sequences. Proline cannot donate the backbone hydrogen bond a beta-strand needs, which is the predicted reason the barrel fails to fold. The recombinant protein is grossly misfolded and none is detected in patient fibroblasts. The ClinVar pathogenic record carries no assertion criteria.

evidence.snippet: The p.Leu175Pro mutation grossly misfolded PLPHP.

nodes.description: c.119C>T. Stability variant. In the model Pro40 opens strand beta-1, is buried (relative accessibility 0.03) and 13.8 angstroms from PLP. The purified protein is folded but less thermostable. ClinVar classifies it as of uncertain significance.

evidence.snippet: PLPHP stability was decreased in p.Arg241Gln, p.Pro40Leu, and p.Arg205Gln mutants (thermofluor assays).

nodes.description: c.260C>T. Stability variant far from the cofactor: in the model Pro87 is 22 angstroms from PLP in an exposed loop (relative accessibility 0.52) between helix alpha-3 and strand beta-4, and it is not conserved (7 of 29 other family sequences). The purified protein is well folded but solubility and yield are reduced. It is the most common pathogenic missense allele in gnomAD v4 (6.3e-05). ClinVar: pathogenic/likely pathogenic.

nodes.description: c.233C>G. Nonsense variant in the third beta/alpha unit; any product lacks 198 of 275 residues, including Ile94, the phosphate-binding turn and Arg241. The founding family's allele: transcript reduced and no protein detected in patient fibroblasts. A null allele.

evidence.snippet: complementation with human PROSC restored growth whereas hPROSC encoding p.Leu175Pro, p.Arg241Gln, and p.Ser78Ter did not.

nodes.description: c.206A>G. Tyr69 follows the PLP-contacting Asn68 and, in the model, is 7.4 angstroms from PLP and surface-exposed (relative accessibility 0.29), unlike the buried pocket variants. The two recombinant studies of this variant disagree. One found extensive disulfide-linked dimerization with reduced PLP content and accessibility. The other found the protein fully saturated with PLP, slightly more thermostable than wild type, and monomeric even without reducing agent, and placed Tyr69 at the dimer interface. Both agree that the protein folds and is stable, so this variant does not act through loss of the protein; how it causes disease is unresolved. It is absent from ClinVar.

nodes.description: c.704T>G. Val235 is the last residue of the C-terminal phosphate-anchoring helix (residues 226-235), 15.6 angstroms from PLP and not conserved. Reported with a favorable cognitive outcome and interpreted as hypomorphic. It is the most common reported allele in gnomAD v4 (2.1e-04, 335 of 1,611,816 alleles, no homozygotes) and ClinVar holds conflicting classifications, so its pathogenicity is less secure than that of the other alleles listed.

nodes.description: c.134T>A. Cofactor-pocket variant. Val45 is on strand beta-1 two residues before the Schiff-base lysine, buried (relative accessibility 0.07), conserved in 24 of 29 other family sequences (the rest are isoleucine or alanine) and 3.8 angstroms from PLP in the model. Aspartate is predicted to put a buried negative charge against the pyridine ring. Experimentally the protein is purified without cofactor and in low yield. It is absent from ClinVar.
